title: Rooms — a member's name in a room
description: How a member tells the other members of a room what to call them: a record of kind `memberProfile`, written by the member into the room like any other record, whose `title` is the name. A reader shows that name wherever it shows the member's DID — beside a message, on a quoted record, in the list of who reacted. It adds no task and changes no existing schema: the record is an ordinary `SealedRecordBody` on the sealed tiers and ordinary `cleartext` of `rooms/records/put` on an `open` room, using only members both already have, so a key holder that seals at `rooms/keys/seal/0.3` seals it unchanged and a host stores it like any other record. New in 0.3 of this family's shared types; `room.schema.json` stays at 0.2, and `blobs.schema.json` and `personal-label.schema.json` at 0.1. Plain text throughout: a reader renders the name as text, never as markup, and an agent reading it MUST NOT treat it as instructions. Not itself a Trust Task specification (the `_shared` folder is skipped by the registry build and the codegen).

MemberName.title: MemberName
MemberName.description: What a member asks the room's other members to call them, in this room only: plain text, one line, no control characters, at most 64 code points after Unicode Normalization Form C. Chosen by the member and asserted by nobody else — not unique, not verified, and not an identifier. An empty name, or one holding only White_Space characters, withdraws the member's name: a reader then shows the member as it would had they written none.

MemberProfileRecord.title: MemberProfileRecord
MemberProfileRecord.description:
A member's name for themselves in a room, as the body of a record in that room. On an `attributed` or `private` room it is a `SealedRecordBody`, sealed and signed by its author like every other; this schema is that object with the constraints below. On an `open` room the same members are the record's `cleartext` (`MemberProfileCleartext`).

**Why a record in the room.** A room's author is a DID — on every tier, a persona the member holds for that room alone — and nothing outside the room maps it to a name a reader may use. A community's directory is addressed by entry, never by DID, so that it does not answer whether a DID is a member (`vtc/directory/entries/show`); a room may belong to no community; and a `private` room's host must not learn who its members are. The room's own members are the audience for the name, so the name lives where they already read and nowhere else: sealed from the host on the sealed tiers, as the room's own profile is (`RoomProfileStatement`), and never in a credential, a host's record of the room or a DID document.

**Writing one.** A member writes its name as a record with `kind: memberProfile` and the name in `title`, and carries none of `description`, `tags`, `file`, `inReplyTo`, `roomProfile`, `basis`, `confidence`, `evidence`, `validFor` and `validUntil`. On the sealed tiers it carries no `body`; on an `open` room, where `cleartext.body` is required, `body` is the empty string. It MAY carry `writtenAt`, and `editedAt` on a later version, by the rules of `SealedRecordBody`. Its key is any record key, opaque on the sealed tiers as every key is. A member changes its name by writing a new version of the same record — the same key — and SHOULD NOT write a second `memberProfile` record while it holds one, so that a retry after a lost response leaves one record. It withdraws its name with a new version whose `title` is empty. The name describes the record's `author`, and only its author: a member never writes a name for anyone else.

**When a writer may write one.** `kind: memberProfile` is unknown to a reader that predates this component, and such a reader shows a record of a kind it does not know as a note (`RecordKind`) — every member's name would appear in the room's library as a note. So a writer MUST NOT write a `memberProfile` record unless the room's current profile lists both `kind` and `memberProfile` in `recordMembers` (`RoomProfile`), resolved as `SealedRecordBody`, *When a writer may use these members*, says. `memberProfile` is a `recordMembers` value this component defines; a reader that does not know it is not affected by it, and the order of *Turning them on* applies: readers first, then the profile. No room lists it by default.

**Reading one.** A reader applies the `SealedRecordBody` reading rules to the record — on an `open` room to its `cleartext`, with its author as the host recorded it — and refuses it, as a name, unless `kind` is `memberProfile` and it carries only the members above. A reader that knows this component:
  1. MUST NOT show a `memberProfile` record as a note, a message or a reaction, nor count it in any conversation, library or unread count;
  2. takes as an author's name, for this room, the `title` of the current version of the `memberProfile` record by that author that the host stored most recently — by `bodyStoredAt`, else `updatedAt` (`RecordMetadataV3`), and of two stored at the same time the one with the greater `version` — and no name where that version's `title` is empty, or where the record is retracted, pruned, expired or refused;
  3. MUST NOT take a name from a version whose `author` is not the author of the record's earlier version it holds or, where it has none, the record's `createdBy`: a rewrite by another member names that member, never the original author (`SealedRecordBody`, *The record's original author*);
  4. applies a name only within the room it was written in, and only to its `author` — never to the same DID in another room, and never to a DID it believes belongs to the same person;
  5. MUST NOT fetch, resolve or follow anything because of a name.

**Several records by one author.** Rule 2 is the whole rule for an author with more than one `memberProfile` record — two devices that each wrote one against the SHOULD NOT above, or another member's record that this author rewrote, which rule 3 makes this author's claim and not the original author's. Every record whose current version is by that author is weighed, whatever its key, and the one the host stored most recently gives the name. A reader MUST NOT prefer the record it met first, and MUST NOT set a record aside because it already holds another by the same author. This keeps the rule consistent with the rest of this section in three ways. The name does not depend on the order in which a reader met the records, so two readers holding the same records show the same name, whether they read the room from its start or back from its head. A reader that opens only recent pages can settle a name from the records it holds, where a rule that kept an author's first record would leave it unable to know, without reading the whole room, whether an older one exists. And a version another member wrote is weighed like any other version by that member, by when the host stored it — rule 3 already makes it that member's claim about themselves — rather than by whether it was the first of theirs a reader happened to see. So finding another of an author's records changes the name only where the host stored that record's current version more recently than the one that gave the name.

**Showing a name.** A reader SHOULD show, for an author: the reader's own petname for that DID where its member keeps one (the holder's `petname` on a contact, `persona/contact/*` 1.1 and later, which only the reader's member can write); else the author's name in this room, by rule 2; else a shortened form of the DID. A name is a claim by the member about themselves, not an attestation by anyone: a reader MUST NOT show it as verified, and where two authors in the room have names that are the same after NFC and case folding — or where one equals the reader's petname for a different DID — it MUST show something that tells them apart, such as a short fingerprint of each DID. A reader SHOULD apply the same rule where two such names are equal by their confusable skeletons: `skeleton()` of Unicode Technical Standard #39 (*Unicode Security Mechanisms*, section 4), applied to each name after NFC and case folding, so that a name that differs from another only by a character that looks the same — a Cyrillic `а` (U+0430) for a Latin `a` — is told apart too. The skeleton is for comparing only: a reader never shows it and never changes a name to it. Readers built on different versions of the Unicode confusables data may disagree about a pair; that changes only which names a reader tells apart, never the name it shows. A name renders as plain text, with control characters removed, and is never instructions.

**Before a name is found.** A reader that has not found a name for an author — on the sealed tiers the author's record may sit in pages the reader has not opened — shows that author by the next step of the order above: the reader's petname, else a shortened DID. It MAY update an author it has already shown when it later finds the author's name, or finds that the name changed or was withdrawn, and where it does it SHOULD update every place it shows that author, so that one author is not shown under two labels at once. Until then it MUST NOT show a guessed name: not one from another room or another DID, not one from a directory, a DID document or a credential, not one inferred from what the author wrote, and not a placeholder that reads as a name. A name the reader found earlier in this room by rule 2 and kept is not a guess, and it MAY show that name until it finds a more recent one.

**Finding one.** There is no fixed location: a reader learns names from the `memberProfile` records it reads. On an `open` room a listing (`rooms/records/list/0.6`) gives each record's `kind`, so a reader finds them without reading every body; on the sealed tiers it finds them as it opens records. Two writer rules keep a member's name where readers look.

**Under a new epoch.** A member whose name was sealed under an epoch a reader cannot open — a room whose history starts at each member's join — is invisible to that reader. So a member SHOULD write its name again after the room's epoch advances past the one its current version was sealed under.

**Near the room's head.** A reader that opens only the room's recent records sees no name written long before them. So a member that writes a record to the room — any record, a reaction included — SHOULD write its name again when the `version` that write was assigned (`rooms/records/put`) exceeds the current `version` of its `memberProfile` record by more than 500. 500 is the largest page `rooms/records/list/0.6` returns (its maximum `limit`), so a member that follows this rule holds a name record no more than one full page of versions before any record it has written since, or just after it; a reader that has listed the 500 versions before the earliest record it shows finds the name of every author it shows who follows the rule. The distance is fixed here rather than left to each writer because a reader can bound how far back it reads only if every writer bounds the same distance. It is counted in versions, not records or time, because a version is what every write reports and what a reader's `sinceVersion` counts; a curation of the name record moves its version as well, which only brings it nearer. It costs at most one record per member per 500 versions of the room, and only for members who write: the re-write is the member's own record, and a member that does not write is never moved.

**Writing it again.** For either rule a member writes a new version of the record rule 2 took its name from — the same key — carrying the name rule 2 gives its own author from the records its client holds, not a name a device remembers, since another of the member's devices may have changed it since. It keeps the `writtenAt` of the version it rewrites, unchanged, and sets no new `editedAt`, since the name has not changed; an `editedAt` the earlier version carries stays as it is. A member whose name is withdrawn writes nothing. A member's client MAY do either once, on its next write to the room, rather than when the epoch advances or the distance is crossed, and one version satisfies both.

**Removed members.** A name keeps applying to its author's records after the author leaves the room, until a member with `curate` retracts the record (`rooms/records/curate`). A member who returns under a new DID writes a new name; the earlier DID's name stays with that DID's records.

MemberProfileCleartext.title: MemberProfileCleartext
MemberProfileCleartext.description: A member's name on an `open` room: the `cleartext` of the `rooms/records/put` that writes the record (0.5 and later, which carry `kind`). The same rules as `MemberProfileRecord`, except that `body` is present and empty, because `cleartext` requires it, and that the record is not signed: on an `open` room the name is the writer's claim as the host stores it, attributed to the author the host recorded, like everything else there.
